lastCompletedStory.title: Fix nested-quote false-positive in extractCommandSubstitutionSpans (Defect B, subsumes CAM-389)

nextStoryContext: US-002 fixed extractCommandSubstitutionSpans (Defect B, CAM-386/389): instead of splicing a matched $(...) span back verbatim, it now routes it through stripQuotedSpans(content.slice(i, end)), creating mutual recursion (function declarations are hoisted, so the forward reference resolves). This strips inert single-quoted comparand-shaped data nested inside a preserved $(...) (e.g. echo "$(grep -c 'X -eq 1' f.ts)") while genuine unquoted content -- including a live git show main: derivation token -- survives recursion untouched (verified via the pre-existing test $(wc -l < "$(git show main:f.ts)") -eq 42 :: ok fixture row, unaffected). Recursion terminates because each round trip only descends into a strictly-smaller nested quoted span. Accepted residual limit (documented inline near extractCommandSubstitutionSpans): a 2+ level nested DOUBLE-quoted command substitution is not fully stripped at the deepest level -- astronomically rare in oracle criteria. Added two new unit tests (one passing-case, one flagged-forms) to test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts and two new fixture rows to oracle-lint-cases.txt (frozen-comparand :: ok :: the inert-nested-data shape, and frozen-comparand :: flag :: its genuine-unquoted-comparison counterpart). All quality gates green (typecheck, bun test 5249 pass, bun run check:all full spine incl. coverage/dead-code/dup/file-size/lint/ci-parity/agents-md). No _ref bump needed (file not near its file-size ceiling; coverage unaffected). CAM-389 (the tracked issue for this exact defect) should be closed by the operator by hand as subsumed, after a CLEAN review -- this is explicitly NOT a worker task. If a future story touches prd-oracle-lint.ts's quote-stripping pipeline again, grep patterns.md for 'CAM-388'/'CAM-386' first -- there is a long, load-bearing history of narrow regex/recursion fixes in this file and each carries a general lesson worth re-reading before editing further.
